key_insight: The transonic flutter boundary folds because elastic-axis placement changes how shock energy transfer balances modal damping, creating multiple flutter speeds at the same Mach number near the dip.
engineering_relevance: This lets designers predict and shift flutter margins by tuning elastic-axis location, with calibrated surrogate models giving fast, reliable stability calls for aeroelastic design.
method: Coupled unsteady Euler simulations of Isogai case A and elastic-axis variants
Gaussian-process surrogate for damping, improved by batch active learning
Split conformal prediction to convert surrogate outputs into distribution-free stability calls
evidence_signal: With 80 simulations, the learned case A boundary correctly labeled 64 of 65 independent runs, and calibrated calls were wrong in at most 1.6% of cases; 193 simulations plus 40 calibration runs mapped the fold across Mach number and elastic-axis position.
watch_item: Time-domain damping labels can fail silently, so the workflow is sensitive to hidden labeling errors and to mean-incidence setup, which shifted the dip flutter speed by 2.8%.
paper_title: How the elastic axis folds the transonic flutter boundary: shock energy transfer and conformally calibrated active learning
